### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `616aacf6a9cdb28984d554a8070a211c` · 2026-09-26T08:27:47Z

(2) agents.md and shell.md: the tool-grant syntax for an agent's capabilities (and run --isolated's grants, which defer to it). Your harness answer left it undecided. ### Architect · Answer

Event: `04c85bb3a99f34be10a3ab7c14c92275` · 2026-09-26T08:28:23Z

> Architect ruling, applies to files.md, agents.md, shell.md and transfer.md.
> 
> (1) files.md, A-23: THE SAME RULE, refuse visibly and report only real fields. The Elixir File API on Redoubt does not emulate POSIX.
> - File.stat / :file.read_file_info report what 9P and the file server actually have: type (from the qid), size, and mtime if the server stores it. access reflects what this connection may do, when the server says so.
> - mode, uid, gid, links, inode and major_device are :undefined. That is within OTP's own file_info type, which allows 'undefined' for exactly these fields, so nothing is invented.
> - File.chmod, File.chown, File.ln_s and File.ln return {:error, :enotsup}.
> - File.write_stat returns {:error, :enotsup} if it carries mode, uid or gid, and applies mtime and atime only.
> - Why: no program should rely on a permission bit that no server enforces. On Redoubt, authority is the capability, never a mode bit.
> - The compatibility cost is stated. Standard-library paths that do arithmetic on mode (File.cp's and cp_r's mode preservation, Mix's executable check) are adjusted in beamlet's platform layer to skip mode, not fed a fake one.
> - The M4 (self-hosted development) test that compiles a Mix project on the box is what catches any caller that breaks. A host or bench test asserts the :undefined fields, and :enotsup from each refused call.
> - transfer.md's SFTP rules cite this section as the one statement of the rule.
> 
> (2) GRANT SYNTAX: DECIDED now; not Open.
> Agent.start takes three option groups:
> - lease: [time:, pages:, processes:, weight:]
> - labels: [...], a separate option, because adding a label needs approval
> - grants: a keyword list of typed terms, the same terms the steward's lease request carries on the wire
> The kinds are closed:
> - read: PATH and write: PATH, each a path in the launcher's namespace. write does not imply read, so name both when both are meant.
> - gateway: NAME, one of the launcher's own gatewayd grants by name, optionally narrowed: {NAME, hosts: [...]}.
> - git: {REMOTE, fetch: true, push: [REF_PATTERN...], force: false}
> - launch: [pages:, processes:, weight:], a sub-budget the agent may start processes in.
> There is nothing free-form. An unknown kind, an unresolvable path, or a term broader than the launcher holds is refused whole by the steward, before any budget exists. There is no 'all' and no wildcard beyond git's ref patterns.
> Example: grants: [read: "~/project", write: "~/project/out", gateway: "model", git: {"origin", fetch: true, push: ["refs/heads/agent/*"]}]
> run --isolated uses the same kinds as flags, one-to-one: --read P, --write P, --gateway N, --git REMOTE[:fetch|:push=PATTERN], --launch pages=..,processes=..,weight=.. . With no flags you get the defaults already ruled: its own budget, the current directory read-only, no network.
> Tests:
> - each kind is refused when broader than the launcher's;
> - an unknown kind is refused;
> - the flags and the keyword list produce the same steward request.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `d0f178ca0c7c6d64ac38baa34a976343` · 2026-09-26T08:28:23Z

> Both decided; the full text went to doc1-userland on this thread.
> (1) The same rule as SFTP: refuse visibly and report only real fields.
> - File.stat gives type, size, mtime (if stored) and access (if the server says). mode, uid, gid, links and inode are :undefined, which OTP's file_info type allows.
> - chmod, chown, ln_s and ln return {:error, :enotsup}. write_stat applies only mtime and atime.
> - Stdlib mode-arithmetic paths (File.cp mode preservation, Mix's executable check) are adjusted in beamlet's platform layer, never fed a fake mode. The M4 on-box Mix compile test catches regressions.
> (2) The grant syntax is decided now, not Open. Agent.start has lease: [...], labels: [...] and grants: a keyword list of closed typed kinds: read, write, gateway, git (remote, fetch, push ref patterns, force) and launch (a sub-budget). These are the same terms as the steward's lease request. Nothing free-form: unknown, unresolvable or broader terms are refused whole. run --isolated maps its flags one-to-one to the same kinds.
